newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India Reliance to import naphtha for new cracker.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance to import naphtha for new cracker.

text.p: India's industry giant Reliance Industries said it will import two million tonnes per year (50,000 barrels-per-day) of high paraffinic naphtha for its new petrochemical cracker complex when it starts operations in December, a company official said on Friday.
"We will import all the requirements," A. Poddar, vice-president of projects at Reliance told Reuters by telephone.
Reliance had earlier planned to obtain half of the two million tonnes it requires from domestic refineries, industry sources had said.
But Poddar said Reliance could not source its naphtha requirements from within India as domestic refineries did not produce the right quality.
India currently has a surplus of naphtha and exports the excess.
"We are looking typically for an Arabian light grade," he said.
The company was talking to a number of suppliers but no term contracts have yet been concluded, he said.
Reliance will seek its first 50,000-tonne cargo of naphtha for delivery in November to the 700,000-tonne-per-year ethylene plant at Hazira in western India, Poddar said.
The plant will start production in December at around 500,000 tonnes a year or 70 percent of its capacity which it plans to maintain for three months, he said.
